newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairies may see inch of rain by Monday.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairies may see inch of rain by Monday.

text.p: Canada's Prairie grainbelt on Thursday was forecast to receive five to 30 mm (0.2 to 1.2 inch) by Monday evening, Environment Canada said.
"Unsteady, unstable conditions are forecast through to Monday night," meteorologist Francois Choquette said.
Central Alberta's grainbelt was forecast to see the most rainfall at 20 to 30 mm with Saskatchewan likely to see the least at five to 10 mm while Manitoba should see 10 to 15 mm.
The Canadian Wheat Board on June 11 cut its wheat yield outlook by 0.5 bushel an acre because of dry conditions on southeastern Prairies but maintained the estimate this week due to light rains.
Typical yields on Prairie wheat range from 30 to 32 bushels per acre and were cut to 29.5 to 31.5 bushels.

Southeast Saskatchewan and southwestern Manitoba farmland usually produces more wheat than the Prairie average at between 32 to 35 bushels an acre because droughts occur less frequently there than in southern Alberta and the land is black soil which is richer than southern Alberta's brown soil, the CWB said.
